content: CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK is held across blocking keyring I/O. `migrate_legacy_key` calls `keyring::has_api_key()` and `keyring::write_api_key(&k)` while the lock is held (same pattern in `strip_verified_keys` / `migrate_search_keys` / `migrate_mcp_server_secrets_locked`). The header comment claims the lock only guards RMW file writes, but in practice lock duration scales with keyring backend latency (e.g. macOS Keychain prompts, Windows Credential Manager, libsecret dbus round-trips). This serializes every config write behind the slowest path and risks re-entrancy if any keyring call ever fires the audit logger from a callback. Either do keyring IO before acquiring the lock (commit in-memory only, then re-verify under lock), or split into per-resource locks.

`write_memory_tuning_at` takes its own `TUNING_WRITE_LOCK` that is independent of `CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK`, so it is not synchronized with `update_config_file` / `add_allowed_dir` / `migrate_*` (which write the same file under `CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK`). Two concurrent writers — e.g. one RMW-updating `evolution` and one RMW-updating `memoryTuning` — both read the same JSON snapshot, then the last writer silently overwrites the other's unrelated field. The header comment defers this as a follow-up, but until it's fixed this is a real last-writer-wins data-loss race on `bot-config.json`. Fold `TUNING_WRITE_LOCK` into `CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK`, or use a single shared lock for the whole config file.

Static array indexed by `slot.index()` panics if any future `KeySlot` variant maps to an index >= 3. `KeySlot::index()` in `types.rs` currently returns 0/1/2 for Llm/Tavily/Brave, but that invariant is implicit — adding a fourth variant will compile cleanly and then panic at runtime the first time `migrate_legacy_keyring_entry` runs. Consider replacing the hardcoded `[AtomicBool; 3]` with a `HashMap<KeySlot, AtomicBool>` or attaching the migrated flag to the slot itself, and assert in tests that the array length matches the variant count.

`debug_assert!` for lock invariants is compiled out under `--release`. If a caller invokes `migrate_config_file_locked` without holding `CONFIG_WRITE_LOCK` in a release build, the assertion is silently dropped and the function runs against unlocked state — racing with `load_config` / `bot_set_config` and potentially corrupting `write_config_atomic`. Either make it a real `assert!`/explicit precondition check, or rename/privatize so only the `#[cfg(test)]` shim and the single locked caller can reach it.

Check-then-act race: `SCHEMA_MIGRATION_CHECKED.load(...)` runs before `try_lock`, so two concurrent callers can both pass the outer gate. The lock holder then performs the migration and sets the flag; the second caller hits `WouldBlock` and returns `Ok(())` assuming the holder did the work — but if the holder's migration *fails* (the `Err` branch leaves the flag unset per the documented contract) the WouldBlock caller silently skips the next chance to retry. Additionally, the `try_lock` fallback silently drops migration without an audit/log line, so a misordered caller (e.g., `load_config` invoked inside an RMW section without first calling `migrate_bot_config_schema_locked`) silently skips the schema bump. Suggest either (a) keeping a small "migration-attempted-this-process" flag separate from "migration-succeeded", or (b) recording the deferred attempt so the next call retries deterministically.

Recovery from `TryLockError::Poisoned` silently reuses the inner guard and continues. A poisoned mutex almost always means the previous holder panicked — silently swallowing that masks real bugs (state corruption, partial writes during the panic). Use `lock()`/`try_lock()` only on a recovered-from-poison mutex after an explicit audit event so the corruption is observable, and avoid keeping the inner guard if you can't prove the protected state is still consistent.

文档声明「带超时调远端」，但实现里 `shared().call_tool(...).await` 直接等待，没有任何 `tokio::time::timeout` 包裹。若 MCP 服务器挂死/网络半开，会一直占住 dispatch 协程、阻塞主 agent 循环的下一轮工具调用，且不会触发任何取消或重试。请要么补上显式 timeout（建议放在 `shared().call_tool` 之外、便于单测 mock），要么明确把超时责任移到 `call_tool` 内并修正文档以避免误导。

content: `spawn_blocking` 的 JoinHandle 在 `.await.unwrap_or_default()` 处把三种性质截然不同的失败吞成空 Vec：(1) spawn_blocking 内部 `load_config` panic；(2) JoinError（线程被取消/关闭）；(3) 配置里没有 `mcp_servers` 字段（`unwrap_or_default()`）。下游 `servers.into_iter().find(...)` 命中 `None` 时统一报「MCP 服务器已被删除」——配置读取故障被伪装成业务状态，模型会按错误的因果链路重发请求，排障与审计均受影响。应区分错误源，至少 spawn_blocking/JoinError 走 error 通道，「配置缺失」单独文案。

Lost-update race: `bot_set_active_model` does an unlocked load → modify → write. The comment on `bot_set_config` explicitly warns that an unlocked load before a locked write creates a lost-update window (concurrent `persist_last_run`/evolution writes can be silently overwritten). This function never acquires `lock_config_write()` at all, so concurrent `bot_set_config` calls, evolution writes, or two rapid `bot_set_active_model` invocations can race and silently destroy each other's edits (settings-page changes, `verified_vendors`, etc.). Acquire the same write lock used in `bot_set_config` around the read-modify-write.

Verification-flag injection via full config replacement: `prune_verified_vendors` never checks `disk.verified_vendors.contains(v)`. The retain closure only verifies that the vendor's (protocol, base_url) signature is consistent between incoming and disk, so any vendor the frontend includes in `incoming.verified_vendors` whose entries already match in both maps will survive — even if it was never tested. This bypasses the stated "test-only" path documented on `bot_test_connection`. The in-file test `prune_verified_vendors_drops_overwritten_missing_and_url_changed` actually demonstrates this: disk has no verified vendors, yet `DeepSeek` is retained because its signature is consistent. Require `disk.verified_vendors.contains(v)` before retaining, or restrict `verified_vendors` mutations to the test command.

Non-atomic credential/config coordination. In `bot_set_config` all keyring writes (api_key, vendor_key, tavily/brave) run *before* `lock_config_write()` and `write_bot_config_file_locked`, so a config-write failure or a concurrent save leaves credentials already changed while `verified_vendors`/config still describe the old state — the opposite of the documented fail-closed intent. `bot_clear_vendor_key` then separately updates `verified_vendors` and deletes the key without any cross-lock, so an in-flight `bot_test_connection` that read the vendor key before deletion can complete after the delete and re-add the vendor to `verified_vendors`, leaving a vendor flagged verified with no key. Additionally `bot_clear_api_key` never invalidates `verified_vendors` for vendors that had no vendor-specific key and relied on the global fallback. Stage all credential mutations under the same config lock and gate verified-flag changes on the same epoch/keyring state used by the probe.

Credential-bearing probe trusts caller-supplied destination. `bot_test_connection` accepts arbitrary `base_url`, `api_format`, and `vendor` from the IPC caller, loads the matching stored credential (vendor key or global fallback), and attaches it as `Authorization: Bearer` / `x-api-key` to a GET against the caller-supplied URL. There is no scheme/host allow-list, no binding to the vendor's persisted endpoint, and `api_format` is only branched on the literal `"anthropic"` — any other value silently gets Bearer auth with no warning. A compromised renderer (or any untrusted IPC caller) can exfiltrate stored credentials to any host. Validate the URL (scheme, allow-listed host or at minimum non-loopback/non-link-local) and require `vendor`'s persisted base_url to match before attaching credentials; treat unknown `api_format` as an error rather than a default.

Keyring errors silently coerced to "no key". Both branches use `keyring::read_api_key().unwrap_or_default()`, discarding locked-keychain / permission-denied / backend-unavailable errors. This contradicts the project's own policy documented on `bot_get_config` ("keyring 真实故障透传 Err，不吞成未配置") and the doc-comment on this function ("全局主 key 读不到（未配置 / 故障）按无 key 探活"). The practical consequence: a locked keychain makes the probe send no credentials, the server returns 401, and `verified_vendors.retain(|x| x != v)` then incorrectly removes the vendor from the verified list — turning an actionable KeyringError into a false-negative authorization decision. Propagate the keyring error with `?` (matching `has_vendor_key`/`has_api_key` earlier in the file) and let the caller decide.

Authorization ordering: the per-tool rule gate (deny/ask) and `skill_on_step` side-effects run *before* the subagent whitelist, so a forbidden tool can still trigger user confirmation prompts and mutate skill counters/records before being rejected. Move the `subagent_ctx` whitelist (and the budget acquire) ahead of `tool_rule_gate`/`skill_on_step`, or ensure they no-op for non-whitelisted names. Also verify the `use_skill` exemption at lines 271/280 cannot indirectly execute a tool that the deny rule blocks.

Cancellation-/panic-unsafe call/return balance: `tool.call` is emitted at function entry but there is no RAII guard (or scoped future combinator) to ensure `tool.return` is written if the future is dropped/panicked during `ask_user_confirm`, the tool body, `execute_mcp_tool`, `trace_sink` recording, or `skill_on_step_post`. Today only the manually-listed early returns are paired; any other abrupt exit leaves a dangling call in the audit log and an inconsistent skill step state. Wrap the post-`tool.call` body in a guard that always emits a final `tool.return` (or use a `defer`-style helper) keyed by the trace's `tool_call_id`.

Sensitive data in audit previews: `args_preview` (tool.call), `preview` (tool.return), and `parse_args` stderr logging (escape_for_log(args,200)) persist up to 80/200 chars of tool input and output without redaction. Tools commonly handle file contents, secrets, tokens, URLs, or PII; writing them to bot.log leaks them to anyone with log access and to log shipping pipelines. Apply redaction (regex on key names, content-type allow/deny) at the `audit::write_event` boundary or strip previews for tools that touch credentials, and downgrade `parse_args` error logging to the structured audit channel so it can be redacted.

Result/Option mapped to misleading status: `commit_and_report` maps `db_upsert_for` errors to `ToolResult::ok` with empty `refs`. Any consumer that decides domain success from `result.status` (skill post-hook, future pipeline stages, UI caches, automation that polls) will treat failed persistence as committed; only the textual error and a single audit event flag the failure. Either return `ToolResult::warn`/`error` so the semantic outcome is observable, or change every `ToolResult::status` consumer to consult the audit stream/result text first.

Allowlist is not an execution boundary. `npx -y @scope/pkg`, `uvx pkg`, `docker run --mount /`, `python script.py` all run arbitrary code/containers; combined with attacker-controlled args (only length-bounded, not shape-checked), checking argv[0] alone gives no real protection. Either treat config as fully trusted or block dangerous arg patterns / use a tighter launcher registry.

`env`/`headers` are documented as secrets but the struct derives `Debug`, so any `format!("{:?}", cfg)`, panic message, error chain, or test assertion prints plaintext secrets. `skip_serializing` only gates disk; add a manual `impl Debug` that redacts env/headers (e.g., prints map length or `<redacted>`).

Two SSRF gaps here: (1) only lexical host is checked — a public-looking domain can resolve (or rebind) to a private IP, and reqwest follows redirects by default, so a 30x to 127.0.0.1 bypasses this gate; ensure the connection layer resolves the destination IP, rejects reserved ranges, and pins/blocks cross-host redirects. (2) The validator accepts URL userinfo (`http://user:pass@host`) and `McpServerConfig.url` is serialized to bot-config.json, leaking embedded credentials to disk — reject any parsed `username`/`password` or mark the field secret.

Either call `find_trim_collisions` here (rejecting the upsert) or move it into `normalize_server`. Same gap applies to duplicate `id`s in `mcp_servers`: there is no list-level uniqueness check, so two entries with the same `id` cause `upsert`/`remove`/`set_enabled` to operate on only one of them while secret slots remain orphaned.

content: OpenOptions.mode(0o600) 只在文件创建时被采用；tmp 文件若已存在（例如上次写流程在 rename 之前崩溃留下），create(true).truncate(true) 会复用旧 inode 并跳过 mode，于是 rename 之后的目标文件继承旧权限（可能 0644），直接破坏本模块声称的「0600 不变式」和注释里的「无 chmod 窗口」承诺。建议：要么 `.create_new(true)` 拒绝复用旧文件（AlreadyExists 时先删再建），要么 open 后用 `f.set_permissions(Permissions::from_mode(0o600))` 显式 chmod 兜底；并在测试中加一条「预先以 0644 创建 tmp，再触发写」的回归。

`bot_effective_params` returns `CommandResult<...>` but the function unconditionally wraps in `Ok(...)`. If `load_config` returns a `Result`, the error is silently swallowed and the user sees defaults without any indication of failure (e.g., corrupted `bot-config.json`). If it returns `BotConfig` directly, the `CommandResult` wrapper is dead and misleading. Either propagate the load error so the settings UI can surface it, or drop the `CommandResult` wrapper since the function cannot fail.

Sync filesystem syscalls inside an async fn on the Tauri runtime. `extract_path_check` walks every task and calls `std::fs::canonicalize` for each bound file on the async worker thread; with N tasks and M bound files this becomes N×M blocking syscalls that stall concurrent commands/events. Either short-circuit by comparing lexical path prefixes before canonicalizing, or move the whole bound-files scan into `spawn_blocking` (matching the `sanitize_task_files_arg` pattern already in this file).
trigger_reload 文档承诺「失败只记审计不回滚配置」，但 spawn 体里 reload_from_config 的结果被直接丢弃，既不写审计也不记日志；同时 JoinHandle 也被丢弃，应用关停时重载可能被中途打断，留下半连接/未释放的 socket。把 JoinHandle 存下来用 abort_handle + 收尾审计，至少与文档一致。

编辑路径下 store_server_secrets 先于 upsert_in_config 执行且若 upsert 失败补偿被故意跳过——但 store_server_secrets 已经把 keyring 里这个 id 对应的 env/headers 覆盖成「新值」。若 upsert_in_config 因为超上限等业务规则失败，配置文件仍保留旧 env/headers，但 keyring 已写入新值，下一次 reload_from_config 把两者合并时会得到混合态（旧 env + 新 secret）。建议编辑路径下也采取"upsert 成功后再 store_server_secrets"，或者在 upsert 失败时把 keyring 回滚到 pre_existing 的旧值。

Race: the check–remove–spawn–insert sequence is not serialized per server. Two concurrent callers (different cfg snapshots, or `call_tool` racing `reload_from_config`) can both pass the fingerprint gate, each spawn its own subprocess, and the second `slots().insert(...)` clobbers the first — or, worse, resurrects a server that reload already removed. The `mark_down` path (see comment below) can likewise overwrite a freshly reconnected slot for the same id. Add per-id in-flight guards (e.g. a `Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>`) or a generation counter on the slot that `ensure_connected`/`mark_down` re-check before mutating.

`mark_down` unconditionally overwrites whatever is in the slot. If a concurrent thread just reconnected with a different config (or the user removed/disabled the server), this stale failure writes `Down` over the fresh `Connected` slot or resurrects a server that should be gone — wiping out a working connection until the next reload. Gate `mark_down` on the slot's current fingerprint (and on the slot being present at all), or skip the write entirely when the slot is no longer "ours".

`Slot::Down` carries no fingerprint, so `ensure_connected`'s fast path can't tell whether the cached failure corresponds to the current `cfg`. Every retry respawns unconditionally even when nothing relevant changed, and `connected_service` cannot distinguish "stale failure" from "current failure" — which is also why `mark_down` overwrites blindly above. Add `fingerprint: u64` to `Down`, populate it on insertion, and have `ensure_connected` / `mark_down` re-check it under the per-id guard.

Silent argument-shape loss: `args.as_object().cloned()` returns `None` for any non-object JSON (array, string, bool, number). A caller passing the wrong shape therefore invokes the tool with no arguments — possibly triggering defaults, no-op behaviour, or side effects — instead of receiving a typed validation error. Reject non-object values explicitly, treating only JSON `null` (and the absence of `args`) as "no arguments".

Only `TransportClosed`/`TransportSend` mark the slot Down. The bare `Err(_)` branch (which includes timeouts and protocol-level errors) leaves the slot `Connected`, so subsequent `call_tool`/`list_all_tools` keep retrying against the same broken service until config changes or a transport-level error finally fires. Mark Down (subject to the fingerprint guard) on repeated protocol errors and on the first timeout, or at minimum force a disconnect+lazy reconnect when this branch is reached.

The comment says "unwrap 让其响亮暴露" (let it surface loudly) but the implementation silently recovers from poison via `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())`. If a panic ever does occur inside a guarded section, the corrupted `HashMap` is then observed by every subsequent locker without any surface signal. Either change the call sites to `.lock().expect("McpManager slots poisoned")` (or `.unwrap()`) to match the documented intent, or update the comment to reflect that poison is intentionally tolerated and accept the resulting loss of invariants. The same contradiction appears in `stderr_ring`, `stderr_tail_snapshot`, and `prune_stderr`.

Arbitrary child stderr lines are concatenated into the error string returned by `ensure_connected`/`call_tool`, surfaced through `McpSlotStatus.error`, and recorded in audit events. A server can echo values from `cfg.env` / header tokens (or anything else) into stderr; this path neither redacts secrets nor restricts which consumer sees the diagnostic. Either sanitize the joined tail (strip `key=value`, bearer tokens, common credential patterns), or restrict stderr-tail visibility to dev / logs and document exactly which surfaces may see it.

The 20-line ring buffer caps only the line count, not the per-line byte size. `BufReader::lines()` allocates the entire line into memory and the loop ignores `next_line()` errors — so (a) a child emitting one very long line (or no `\n` at all) balloons `VecDeque` entries and the same bytes are then copied verbatim into `format_with_stderr_tail` / audit / IPC; (b) a non-UTF-8 byte sequence returns `Err` from `next_line()`, the loop terminates, and all subsequent stderr from that child is silently discarded. Truncate each entry (e.g. to 4 KiB) on push, and on the error path log + continue (or use `read_until(b'\n', ...)` with a max-buffer cap) instead of dropping the reader.

The HTTP branch delegates all egress protection to `http_url_is_public` and disables redirects, but `reqwest::Client::builder()` still honors `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` by default, and the URL check is performed before `reqwest` resolves DNS. Confirm the helper (a) rejects DNS names that resolve to loopback / private / link-local addresses, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`), and (b) the resolved peer is pinned against the URL host — otherwise DNS-rebinding can still hit a private address. If the helper is purely textual, pre-resolve via `tokio::net::lookup_host`, re-check, and `.resolve(...)` against the reqwest client.

Fallback for missing/unreadable vendor key may leak an unrelated vendor's credential into the override entry's base_url: `crate::bot::read_llm_key(api_provider, active_model_id, models_by_provider)` does NOT return the global main key — it first resolves the *currently active* model's vendor and uses that vendor's key (keyring.rs::read_llm_key ~640). So a per-card override whose vendor key fails to read (or never existed) gets the active vendor's key sent to the override entry's endpoint, which can be a different provider entirely. The comment "全局 key 兜底" is therefore inaccurate; use `crate::bot::read_api_key()` (or a small wrapper that explicitly walks vendor → global main key → vendor-of-selected-entry) instead.

`#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` on `ResolvedModel` exposes `api_key` (cleartext) through any future `dbg!` / `{:?}` / `unwrap()` panic message that includes this struct, and through log crates that auto-format Debug. `BotConfig` deliberately avoids `Debug` for this reason; `ResolvedModel` should redact `api_key` (custom Debug that prints `api_key: "<redacted, len=N>"`) or drop the derive. Combined with the fallback bug above, this is a realistic leak path.

Screenshot filename race: `chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis()` truncates to millisecond precision, so two concurrent `tool_screenshot` invocations within the same millisecond produce identical `wm-screen-<ts>.png` names and silently overwrite each other on disk. The later caller reports a path/file that no longer corresponds to its own screenshot (and any concurrent model consumption of the older path gets corrupt bytes). Append a sub-millisecond counter, atomic file create (`create_new`), or a random suffix to `screenshot_filename` so collisions cannot overwrite an existing artifact.

DNS rebinding / TOCTOU between validation and browser open: `ensure_public_http_url` resolves the host once and rejects loopback/private IPs, but the validated URL string is then handed to `app.opener().open_url`, where the OS browser performs its own (typically later) DNS lookup. An attacker-controlled DNS record that returns a public IP at validation time and a private/loopback IP at browser-open time will bypass the public-net gate and open an internal address. The sandbox comment promises "DNS 解析后拒绝本机/内网/保留地址", so this gap undermines that guarantee — pin the resolved IP into the URL or use a host allowlist/canonical name rather than relying on re-resolution by the browser.

`is_error` classification passes empty tool name. `crate::audit::tool_call_failed("", &text)` is called with an empty string for the tool name argument. If the function inspects the name for per-tool failure semantics (e.g., only flagging specific tools as failures, or excluding certain error-text-only results), passing "" silently misclassifies every tool result. The block currently has access to `tool_use_id`; the matched tool_use's `name` (from the `emitted_tool_use_ids` tracking step) should be threaded through so `tool_call_failed` gets the actual tool name it was designed to inspect. As-is, this is either a silent misclassification or a misuse of the audit API.

`existed` check OR's `is_dir` and `is_file`. If `canonical` resolves to a directory (e.g., user passes a directory path that survives `resolve_writable` because the parent is writable), `existed = true` triggers the "覆盖已存在文件" confirmation branch, then `atomic_write` fails with `IsADirectory` (an opaque IO error). The intent appears to be "is there an existing file to overwrite" — should be `is_file` only (and `resolve_writable` should arguably reject directory targets as a separate hardening).

Per-tool `Allow` ToolRuleAction bypasses the whitelist check **and** the `perm_mode` triage entirely — it only emits an audit log. In `resolve_with_perm`, an `allow` rule for any tool means the model can read **any** canonical-resolvable path (including symlink-resolved escapes that fall outside every whitelist dir) without user confirmation. The comment says "rule_allow = 单工具 yolo" so this appears intentional, but worth confirming: (a) rule persistence/sanitization is hardened, (b) rule auth requires the same trust level as `perm_mode=Yolo`, and (c) `Deny` rules should still take precedence over an `Allow` for a different tool if a future refactor reorders checks.

Same per-tool `Allow` bypass exists in the **write** path: a single `allow` rule for `edit_file` / `write_file` lets the model write to any path the OS resolves, completely sidestepping `writable_dirs` and the `ask_user_confirm` danger prompt. The "覆盖已存在文件" sub-prompt is also bypassed by an Allow rule because `existed` branch sits above this check (actually below — `resolve_writable` returns before the existed check, but the cover-prompt logic still runs and emits its own confirmation). Verify the comment "与读侧同语义" matches the actual UX: does the user expect a per-tool Allow to mean "no whitelist, no confirm, ever" for writes? If yes, document it; if no, also gate the cover-prompt behind `rule.allow`.
